vectors.name: deviation-float-binary64-not-shortest-accepted
vectors.note: 1.5 as binary64, which §6.3.1 requires. RFC 8949 §4.2.1's shortest-float rule requires binary16 here — so a stock canonical encoder never produces these bytes for this value, and a host built on one fails this vector.

vectors.name: deviation-float-shortest-form-refused
vectors.note: The same 1.5, encoded exactly as RFC 8949 §4.2.1 mandates. A host that decodes with a stock canonical CBOR library accepts this and diverges from every conforming host on the first float it sees. The data model has one float type, and shortest-float would make a value's encoded width depend on its magnitude.

vectors.name: deviation-keys-ordered-by-content-accepted
vectors.note: "aa" before "z", which is content order: 0x6161 < 0x7a. RFC 8949 §4.2.1 orders keys by their *encoded* bytes, where the length byte leads — 0x617a ("z") < 0x626161 ("aa") — so a stock canonical encoder emits the other order and a host built on one rejects these bytes as unsorted.

vectors.name: deviation-keys-ordered-by-encoding-refused
vectors.note: The same signal in RFC 8949 §4.2.1's order. Ordering by content gives the platform one ordering — the same one EXPR §2 exposes as map iteration order and §7.5's (keys m) returns — so a value's key order does not change between the wire and the language.
